summary: Hale Peak lookout on the west shore of Harrison Lake, BC; early-20th-century origin, a 2015 fire spared it, and sources disagree on whether the tower is original or a replica.

facts.design: Lookout tower on Hale Peak; sources disagree on whether the standing structure is the original or an exact replica
facts.status_note: A hiking club post says members helped dismantle the old tower and rebuild an exact replica; a directory says it survived a wildfire and was refurbished; a site listing says the original structure was renovated

access.note: Hiking trail from a service road off the Harrison West Service Road, parking on the road shoulder; no closure or ownership detail found; interior access not confirmed in sources

visit.trail_note: Out-and-back hike; sources give 3.5 km or 4 km and 337 m or 415 m of climbing; the listing warns the area is heavily populated with ticks

events.note: Human-caused fire that left soot and ash on the trees; a hiking post says the old tower escaped its flames

notes_for_editor: No official source was read. The Recreation Sites and Trails BC agency named in the record was not confirmed by any page read, so no agency fact is included. Searches found no government record, and the sources read were travel and hiking pages. Summit height is unsettled: 701 m (Firelookout.ca), 717 m (peak-bagging page) and 739 m (hiking post, which may mean the highest point). Trail stats conflict (3.5 km and 337 m of climb versus 4 km and 415 m). Whether the standing tower is original, renovated or a rebuilt replica is not settled; the replica claim is undated ('last year' in the post). No build year appears in any source, so there is no built event. The 2015 fire is in one hiking post only. Interior access is not confirmed. Firelookout.ca's record has N/A for tower type, height and year. Snippets from AllTrails, Adventures in Elevation and Tourism Harrison were seen but not read, so they are not cited. No new photos.
